p: אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַךְ מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים לג, א).
מָצִינוּ בְּבִרְכַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
We find regarding the blessing of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
"'Of the dew of the heavens' — this is Scripture;
'and of the fatness of the earth' — this is Mishnah," etc.;
that Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him, would bless
And all the more so Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
as we say (in the Shabbos morning prayer):
"Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion";
and all the time that he was
they were free only for Torah
(and as they said in the Mechilta (Beshalach, Vayassa 3)
only to those who ate the manna");
and had he entered Eretz Yisrael,
it would always have been so,
that their work would be done
and they would be free for Torah,
and not in matters of this world.
they expounded "And this is for Yehudah" (Devarim 33:7):
"and You shall be a help against his adversaries" (ibid.).
and Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
תּוֹרָה צִוָּה לָנוּ מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם לג, ד).
And where do we find that Moshe commanded?
the words of Hashem, may He be blessed?
It would have been fitting to say
"the portion of the lawgiver is hidden."
And in Malachi, where it is written (Malachi 3:22),
"which I commanded him at Chorev" etc.
regarding what they said in the Gemara (Menachos 29b):
"It is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai";
why his mind was set at ease
by this halachah that he heard,
that he said it is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai,
יוֹתֵר מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁדָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
more than everything Rabbi Akiva expounded,
what he drew out of the Written Torah,
which he knew that he himself had brought down to earth.
and did not know what was being said,
even though Rabbi Akiva's students understood,
and in this there was no portion
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who was good from the outset,
for when he was born the house filled with light
in that he brought forth the halachos
that are for us halachah to Moshe from Sinai,
like a halachah to Moshe from Sinai?";
and likewise on "a halachah without a reason"
such that there is no need to give a reason for it."
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
devised them from his own reasoning,
and they were halachah to Moshe from Sinai,
for the power was given to him from Sinai
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים לח, א):
and in the manner of what they said (Nedarim 38a):
that he devised them through his reasoning.
for Moshe was more humble than any man,
וְהוּא זָכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי הָעֲנָוָה,
and he merited this through humility,
"And wisdom — from where, ayin, shall it be found?"
And this is "Moshe commanded us the Torah":
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
"Whereas Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
"An inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov" —
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט, ג)
in the manner of what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 9:3)
that is, since he did not find him learned
either in Scripture or in Mishnah,
that he needed to be supported like a dog,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ח, א)
in the manner of what they said (Bava Basra 8a)
who did not wish to benefit
from the honor of the Torah
"Support me like a dog and like a raven."
"'An inheritance of the congregation of Yannai'
but rather 'of the congregation of Yaakov.'"
That is, every single one of Yisrael
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא לג, ב)
and as they expounded in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 33b)
"and to the house of Yaakov their sins" (Yeshayahu 58:1):
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא קַמָּא צב, א)
And as we find in the Gemara (Bava Kamma 92a):
and even though they speak mere talk,
they found the words in a verse,
for this is their portion in words of Torah.
And this is "an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov":
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
to every single one of Yisrael,
who gave him the taste of the verse
וְאַף שֶׁרַבִּי יַנַּאי יָדַע גַּם כֵּן
and although Rabbi Yannai also knew
that "the congregation of Yaakov" is written,
until he heard from the guest,
קְהִלַּת יַנַּאי אֵין כָּתוּב כָּאן וְכוּלֵּי,
"'The congregation of Yannai' is not written here," etc.;
for this was his portion in the Torah.
And as our holy Rebbe said,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the righteous and holy be for a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
on what they said in the Midrash
"All my days I would read the verse
מִי הָאִישׁ הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים (תְּהִלִּים לד, יג).
'Who is the man who desires life?'" (Tehillim 34:13).
the verse as it is written,
yet when he heard it from him
which he had never sensed before.
And this is because this was
which is the tastes of Torah:
that is in words of Torah.
